_note: Public literature-map groups. The kind field distinguishes intellectual lineages, research traditions, conceptual and methodological frameworks, research infrastructure, and evidence context.

traditions.name: Phenomenology, Hermeneutics, and the Lifeworld
traditions.contribution: Connects phenomenology's attention to lived experience with Gadamer's philosophical hermeneutics and Virilio's critique of technologically accelerated perception. Grounds existential abstraction while keeping interpretation and the lifeworld explicit.

traditions.name: Learning Sciences of Productive Struggle
traditions.contribution: Supplies the empirical engine: desirable difficulty, productive failure, and retrieval practice show that durable learning requires the very effort that frictionless AI removes.

traditions.name: Canadian Media Theory
traditions.contribution: Establishes that media carry biases of time and space and that the medium reshapes perception. The upstream source for media ecology and for reading AI as an environment, not a tool.

traditions.name: Critical Theory of Technology
traditions.contribution: Argues that technical systems encode values and tend toward efficiency at the expense of judgment. Frames pedagogical friction as a deliberate, democratic intervention.

traditions.name: Constructionism
traditions.contribution: Holds that powerful ideas are built through making and debugging. A direct counterweight to answer-generation: the struggle is where the learning lives.

traditions.name: Media Ecology (Ong)
traditions.contribution: The conceptual spine. Ong's account of how writing and print restructure consciousness is extended here past secondary orality into algorithmic secondary orality and tertiary algorithmicity.

traditions.name: Constructivist Qualitative Inquiry
traditions.contribution: Supplies the study's interpretive stance for understanding participant meaning as situated and co-constructed. Reflexive thematic analysis is grouped here because this study uses it within that constructivist stance; the method itself remains theoretically flexible.

traditions.name: Media Archaeology
traditions.contribution: Reads media materially and across deep time, privileging circuits and code over content. Situates AI within long genealogies rather than as a clean rupture.

traditions.name: Educational Sensemaking
traditions.contribution: Explains how educators and school systems interpret ambiguous conditions through existing frames, professional communities, and local practice rather than through policy text alone. Supplies the account of teacher and leader sensemaking that the research questions ask about directly.

traditions.name: Truth, Language, and Epistemic Integrity
traditions.contribution: Clarifies the difference between lying and indifference to truth. Gives the dissertation a vocabulary for examining fluent AI output, authorship, and rhetorical responsibility without treating Frankfurt's conceptual analysis as phenomenology.

traditions.name: Research Design, Analysis, and Software
traditions.contribution: The study's research infrastructure: convergent mixed-methods design, integration through joint displays, coding and sampling guidance, cognitive interviewing, scale development, and statistical software. Supports how the study is conducted rather than naming an intellectual lineage.

traditions.name: Tertiary Orality Scholarship
traditions.contribution: The existing scholarly attempt to name what follows secondary orality, across voice queries, spoken computer-mediated communication, virtual reality, and documents as dialogue. This is the conversation tertiary algorithmicity enters and revises, so the dissertation's central move is legible as an intervention rather than a coinage.

traditions.name: Stieglerian Critique
traditions.contribution: Diagnoses cognitive proletarianization: the externalization of memory and skill to systems. The case for reclaiming cognitive craft.

traditions.name: Critical Algorithm Studies
traditions.contribution: Shows how curation and personalization quietly govern what reaches whom. Anchors algorithmic secondary orality and the infrastructural dimension of friction.

traditions.name: Attention, Deep Reading, and Embodiment
traditions.contribution: Documents how digital and algorithmic environments erode deep reading, attention, resilience, and authentic dialogue. The human stakes of frictionless production.

traditions.name: Disability, Access, and Exclusionary Difficulty
traditions.contribution: Names how difficulty is distributed unequally and how ableist norms make some barriers read as rigor. Disciplines the productive-versus-exclusionary distinction so that preserving friction never becomes a defense of exclusion.

traditions.name: Surveillance Capitalism and Platform Power
traditions.contribution: Names the political economy behind algorithmic systems: data extraction, behavioral prediction, and rent. Locates friction as the defense of cognitive sovereignty.

traditions.name: Postdigital and Critical Literacies
traditions.contribution: Treats the analog and digital as entangled and reframes literacy as critical, creative, and justice-oriented. Supports the productive-versus-exclusionary friction distinction.

traditions.name: Generative AI in Education: Evidence and Practice Context
traditions.contribution: Brings together contemporary empirical studies, national indicators, policy and practice resources, assessment redesign, and AI scaffolding. It maps the context the dissertation studies rather than claiming a single intellectual lineage.
